protocol.probes: checkpoint proj on held-out tokens (2,048), fixed before any update

support_stats.rng: torch.Generator('cpu') (mt19937) seeded per purpose / chunk with sha256-derived 63-bit seeds; permutation = stable argsort of int64 keys uniform in [0, 2^62); ties -> lower local position
support_stats.tie_break: TopK: stable descending sort; cover repair: lexicographic (j, u, d); quota repair: lexicographic (j, u, d)
support_stats.quota_rule: b = floor(k m / 64), h = k m - 64 b; first h positions of the keyed permutation key_seed(Balanced-TopK, 16, graph1, layout0, quota, perm, <chunk>) get b + 1
support_stats.importance: a[u, j] = sum_valid c W_pre[u, c, j]^2 (FP64, sequential over c)
support_stats.score: sum_{j in A} a[u, j] (FP64, ascending coordinate order)

bf16_rounding.note: stored = BF16(round-to-nearest(s_i * w)); the FP32 product is exact for power-of-two s_i

normalization.rule:
For independent equal-variance inputs Var(z_i - b_i) = sigma_x^2 sum_k w_ik^2, so pruning a row to k_i of its 64
envelope inputs lowers its input-driven variance without proving the row useless.  Treatments (the mask, the bias
count and the optimizer budget are unchanged; the scale multiplies EVERY retained weight of the row exactly once
-- backbone and tile coordinates of a hybrid support are one dense masked row, so an overlap is never scaled
twice; structural zeros stay zero; disconnected rows (k_i = 0) stay all-zero):
